items.title: Israel renews Beirut bombardment, killing 3 including child

featured_image.name: Beirut under fire as Israel expands air strikes in Lebanon

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the town of Bchamoun, about 10 kilometers southeast of central Beirut, killed at least three people including a three-year-old girl early Tuesday, Lebanon's Health Ministry said. Five others were wounded in the predawn attack, which came as Israel renewed its bombardment of the Lebanese capital after a two-day lull.[1][2]

Online footage showed flames engulfing at least one apartment in the struck building. The attack on Bchamoun, located in the Aley district of Mount Lebanon, hit outside the southern suburbs of Beirut where Israel had previously ordered evacuations and concentrated its strikes against Hezbollah.[2][1]

items.title: Moldova declares 60-day energy emergency after Russian strikes sever key power line

featured_image.name: Moldova imposes 60-day energy emergency after Russian strikes in Ukraine cut key power line

items.description:
Moldova's parliament voted on Tuesday to impose a 60-day state of emergency in the country's energy sector after overnight Russian drone strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure severed the high-voltage Isaccea-Vulcănești power line, the primary conduit for electricity imports from Romania.[1][2]

Seventy-two lawmakers in the 101-seat legislature approved the measure, with no votes against and 18 abstentions, according to the Associated Press. The emergency is set to take effect on Wednesday, March 25.[3][4][1]

featured_image.name: Photos of missiles over Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in a ...

items.description: Iran launched multiple waves of missiles at Israel on Tuesday, striking central Tel Aviv and triggering sirens across the country, as a separate U.S. airstrike in western Iraq killed a senior commander of the Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces. The dual escalations came even as President Donald Trump claimed diplomatic progress with Tehran — assertions Iran dismissed as "false news."

items.title: Oil whipsaws as Trump's Hormuz deadline passes without action

featured_image.name: UN maritime body starts talks on Middle East shipping with Hormuz strait  effectively closed

items.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial shipping nearly a month after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the blockade, leaving global oil markets volatile and prediction markets signaling that disruptions could persist well into spring. Brent crude has surged roughly 55% from pre-war levels, while a draft UN Security Council resolution authorizing the use of force to reopen the waterway has introduced a new diplomatic front to the crisis.[1]

items.title: Iran tells IMO that 'non-hostile' ships may transit Hormuz

featured_image.name: Only a handful of ships risk Strait of Hormuz transit — who ...

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Tuesday circulated a letter to International Maritime Organization member states declaring that "non-hostile vessels" may transit the Strait of Hormuz provided they coordinate with Iranian authorities, according to the Financial Times. Vessels linked to the United States, Israel, and what Tehran called "other participants in the aggression" are explicitly excluded from passage.[1][2][3]

items.title: 15-point US ceasefire proposal for Iran war emerges

items.description: Israel's Channel 12 on Tuesday published a 15-point U.S. document reportedly being developed to halt the war with Iran, outlining sweeping demands for Tehran to dismantle its nuclear capabilities in exchange for sanctions relief. The proposal, which envisions a one-month ceasefire during which a broader framework agreement would be negotiated, comes as the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fourth week amid contradictory signals from Washington and Tehran about whether talks are even taking place.[1]

items.title: Trump extends Iran deadline as Strait of Hormuz remains closed to shipping

featured_image.name: Trump considers "winding down" Iran war without opening Hormuz Strait

items.description: Nearly four weeks after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut to international shipping, with prediction markets, corporate leaders, and diplomats all pointing to a resolution that could take weeks or months to materialize. President Donald Trump on Monday extended by five days a deadline for Iran to reopen the waterway, citing "very good and productive conversations" — claims Tehran promptly denied.[1][2]

items.title: US awaits Iran's response on proposed Thursday peace summit

featured_image.name: Pakistan to Host First US-Iran Talks Since War Began

items.description:
The United States and regional mediators are waiting on Tehran's answer to a proposed high-level peace summit that could take place as early as Thursday, even as the month-old war continues and the Pentagon prepares to send thousands more troops to the Middle East.

Two sources with knowledge of the discussions told Axios that Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey have been passing messages between Washington and Tehran, with Pakistan offering to host the talks in Islamabad. President Trump shared Pakistan's offer on Truth Social, signaling his interest in making a summit happen. If plans firm up, Vice President JD Vance is expected to represent the U.S. side, potentially facing Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, whom the White House views as its highest-level potential counterpart in Tehran.[1][2][3]
